title: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS: what each model delivers and what is left to you

videos.script: Somebody tells you the shop has moved to the cloud. It sounds like an answer. It is really a question. {{cloud}} The shop still runs on a computer, in a building. That computer has an operating system that needs patches, and a database that needs backups. Someone has to do each of those jobs. The question is who. {{stack}} This lesson draws the jobs as a stack of layers, from the building at the bottom to your data at the top. Then it draws one line across the stack. Below the line, the provider does the work. Above it, you do. {{line}} The three names you will hear, IaaS, PaaS and SaaS, are three heights for that line. Rent a virtual machine, and the line is low. The operating system is yours. Hand over your code to a platform, and the line is higher. Use a finished application, and it is almost at the top. {{models}} Almost, because two things never cross it. Your data, and who is allowed to reach it, stay yours in every model. {{yours}} By the end, you can take the name of any cloud service and place it on that line. You will know which jobs it takes off your hands, and which it leaves with you. Every price you see in this course is a line of a published price list, and nothing here needed a cloud account. {{end}}
